summary: The bill makes it a federal crime, punishable by up to 10 years in prison, for any registered sex offender to obtain a child through surrogacy or enter a surrogacy contract as an intended parent, and bars federal courts from enforcing such contracts.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budget allocations of any kind.
The bill does not address taxes, tax rates, deductions, or any revenue-related measures.

While surrogacy involves medical procedures, the bill focuses exclusively on prohibiting sex offenders from using surrogacy arrangements and does not regulate healthcare delivery, coverage, or markets.
No provisions relate to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill references interstate and foreign commerce in jurisdictional hooks but does not alter immigration pathways, visas, border policy, or protections for noncitizens.
The bill makes no reference to abortion, reproductive rights, or pregnancy termination.
No connection to military, defense budgets, or national security spending.
The legislation has no environmental, regulatory, or climate-related content.
No provisions affect welfare programs, entitlements, or social assistance.
The bill does not address schools, education funding, or school choice.
No references to controlled substances, decriminalization, or drug enforcement.

The bill adds a new federal criminal prohibition (18 U.S.C. § 2260B) making it a felony for registered sex offenders to obtain a child via surrogacy, punishable by up to 10 years imprisonment and fines. It also bars enforcement of related contracts. This expands criminal liability and penalties in a narrow area, aligning modestly with tougher enforcement rather than rehabilitation-focused reforms.
Jurisdictional language references foreign commerce but the bill does not enact tariffs, trade agreements, or protectionist measures.
No fiscal, deficit, or debt-reduction provisions appear in the text.

The bill defines 'female' in biological terms and restricts sex offenders (regardless of orientation) from surrogacy, but it does not expand or limit legal protections specifically for LGBTQ+ individuals.
The legislation contains no foreign aid authorizations or restrictions.
No election administration, voting access, or campaign-related content.
No data privacy, technology regulation, or surveillance provisions.
The bill does not address employment, worker rights, or union matters.
No religious exemptions, anti-discrimination rules, or conscience protections are included.
